neighbours.label: demonstrative (this, these, that, neither) pointing back to a claim or notion being evaluated or refuted
fire: Many people think the full moon makes hospitals busier. Researchers have tested this and found no effect.
Some say that cold weather causes colds, but doctors have long argued against this idea.
There are two common myths about sharks. Neither of these is supported by the data.
It was once believed that the brain stops growing in childhood. Modern imaging has overturned this.
Critics claim the tax will hurt small shops. Economists have examined these claims closely.
Older textbooks describe a fixed tongue map of tastes. That model has since been abandoned.
Some fans insist the stadium is cursed. Historians dismiss this as a story invented by reporters.
The rumour said the factory would close in May. Management denied this the next morning.
quiet: Many people think the full moon makes hospitals busier. Researchers measured admissions for ten years.
Some say that cold weather causes colds, but doctors point to viruses spread indoors.
There are two common myths about sharks. Sharks rarely attack people at all.
It was once believed that the brain stops growing in childhood. Modern imaging shows lifelong change.
Critics claim the tax will hurt small shops. Economists studied shop revenues in three cities.
Older textbooks describe a fixed tongue map of tastes. Taste buds sense every flavour everywhere.
Some fans insist the stadium is cursed. Historians point to the team's poor coaching instead.
The rumour said the factory would close in May. Management held a meeting the next morning.

notes: Card top: Neither (of these stereotypes), investigated these (notions), against this notion, destroyed this, that model. The - pole's output suppresses 'fact'. Near misses state the same arguments naming the claim with a full noun phrase instead of a demonstrative.
